   958:     issues: List[GovernanceIssue] = []
   959: 
   960:     issues.extend(detect_upload_structure_drift(workspace_id))
   961:     issues.extend(detect_upload_phrase_pool_drift(workspace_id))
   962:     issues.extend(detect_active_phrase_set_drift(workspace_id))
   963:     issues.extend(detect_active_phrase_pool_drift(workspace_id))

   968:         issue for issue in issues
   969:         if issue.status in {DRIFTED, REPAIR_REQUIRED}
   970:     ]
   971: 
   972:     info_issues = [
   973:         issue for issue in issues
   974:         if issue.status == INFO
   975:     ]
   976: 
   977:     drift_detected = len(blocking_issues) > 0
   978:     info_detected = len(info_issues) > 0
   979: 
   980:     status = classify_workspace_status(blocking_issues)
   981: 
   982:     if not drift_detected:
   983:         status = HEALTHY
   984: 
   985:     report = {
   986:         "workspace_id": workspace_id,
   987:         "status": status,
   988:         "health_score": score_for_status(status),
   989:         "drift_detected": drift_detected,
   990:         "info_detected": info_detected,
   991:         "issue_count": len(issues),
   992:         "blocking_issue_count": len(blocking_issues),
   993:         "info_issue_count": len(info_issues),
   994:         "issues": [asdict(issue) for issue in issues],
   995:         "recommended_action": recommended_action_for_status(status),

   171: def _sha256_file(
   172:     path: Path,
   173: ) -> str:
   174:     digest = hashlib.sha256()
   175: 
   176:     with path.open("rb") as handle:
   177:         for block in iter(
   178:             lambda: handle.read(
   179:                 1024 * 1024
   180:             ),
   181:             b"",
   182:         ):
   183:             digest.update(block)
   184: 
   185:     return digest.hexdigest()

   471: def _extract_docx_paragraphs_v2(path: str | Path) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
   472:     """Extract paragraphs WITH their style ids from word/document.xml.
   473: 
   474:     FIXES vs v1:
   475:     - <w:br/>, <w:cr/> become line breaks and <w:tab/> becomes a space
   476:       inside a paragraph (previously 'line one<w:br/>line two' extracted
   477:       as 'line oneline two').
   478:     - The paragraph style id (<w:pStyle w:val="Heading1"/>) is captured so
   479:       heading detection can be STYLE-BASED, consistent with the strict
   480:       style-based approach used elsewhere in the system (files.py).
   481:     """
   482:     from zipfile import ZipFile
   483:     import html as html_lib
   484: 
   485:     p = Path(path)
   486: 
   487:     with ZipFile(p) as z:
   488:         xml = z.read("word/document.xml").decode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
   489: 
   490:     paragraphs: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
   491: 
   492:     for paragraph_xml in _DOCX_P_RE.findall(xml):
   493:         style_m = _DOCX_PSTYLE_RE.search(paragraph_xml)
   494:         style_id = style_m.group(1).strip() if style_m else ""
   495: 
   496:         # Convert breaks/tabs to whitespace BEFORE pulling runs, so the
   497:         # boundary survives run concatenation.
   498:         pxml = _DOCX_BR_TAB_RE.sub(
   499:             lambda m: "\n" if "tab" not in m.group(0).lower() else " ",
   500:             paragraph_xml,
   501:         )
   502: 
   503:         parts: List[str] = []
   504:         pos = 0
   505:         # Walk the paragraph xml preserving order of text runs and the
   506:         # injected \n markers between them.
   507:         for m in _DOCX_T_RE.finditer(pxml):
   508:             gap = pxml[pos:m.start()]
   509:             if "\n" in gap:
   510:                 parts.append("\n")
   511:             parts.append(html_lib.unescape(m.group(1)))
   512:             pos = m.end()
   513:         if "\n" in pxml[pos:]:
   514:             parts.append("\n")
   515: 
   516:         text = "".join(parts)
   517:         # Normalize within the paragraph but keep internal line breaks.
   518:         lines = [" ".join(l.split()) for l in text.split("\n")]
   519:         text = "\n".join(l for l in lines if l).strip()
   520: 
   521:         if text:
   522:             paragraphs.append({"text": text, "style_id": style_id})

   117: def _paragraphs_from_content_body(content_body: str) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
   118:     """Split content_body into paragraphs on blank lines.
   119: 
   120:     Contract with upload_document_extractor: extracted text preserves
   121:     paragraph boundaries as blank lines ("\\n\\n").
   122: 
   123:     Each paragraph now also carries start_char/end_char offsets into
   124:     content_body so downstream consumers can locate paragraphs without
   125:     re-searching (and so future schema versions can drop the duplicated
   126:     text in favor of offsets).
   127:     """
   128:     raw = str(content_body or "")
   129:     paragraphs: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
   130: 
   131:     idx = 0
   132:     for i, m in enumerate(re.finditer(r"[^\n]+(?:\n(?!\n)[^\n]*)*", raw), start=1):
   133:         block = m.group(0).strip()
   134:         if not block:
   135:             continue
   136:         idx += 1
   137:         paragraphs.append(
   138:             {

   106: def enqueue_job(job_id: str) -> bool:
   107:     """Kept for API compatibility.
   108: 
   109:     Enqueueing is now implicit: create_job persists the job with status
   110:     JOB_STATUS_QUEUED, and that persisted status is the queue membership.
   111:     This function only verifies the job actually exists in a queued state,
   112:     which catches caller bugs (e.g. enqueueing an ID that was never created).
   113:     """
   114:     job = get_job(job_id)
   115:     return job is not None and job.status == JOB_STATUS_QUEUED
   116: 
   117: 
   118: def dequeue_job(worker_id: str | None = None) -> Optional[OrchestrationJob]:
   119:     """Atomically claim and return the highest-priority queued job.
   120: 
   121:     The returned job has ALREADY been transitioned to JOB_STATUS_RUNNING
   122:     (with claim metadata) under a cross-process lock, so no other worker
   123:     can receive the same job. Returns None when nothing is queued.
   124: 
   125:     Workers may still call mark_job_running() afterwards; with the
   126:     corrected service.py that call is idempotent.
   127:     """
   128:     with _dequeue_lock():
   129:         for candidate in _queued_jobs():
   130:             metadata: Dict[str, object] = {"claimed_by_dequeue": True}
   131:             if worker_id:
   132:                 metadata["worker_id"] = worker_id
   133:             try:
   134:                 claimed = update_job_status(
   135:                     candidate.job_id,
   136:                     JOB_STATUS_RUNNING,
   137:                     metadata=metadata,
   138:                 )
   139:             except Exception:
   140:                 # Job vanished or store hiccuped between read and write â€”
   141:                 # skip it and try the next candidate rather than failing
   142:                 # the whole dequeue.
   143:                 continue
   144:             return claimed
   145:         return None

     1: // Lightweight loader + resolver for Entity Map (fallbacks-only friendly)
     2: export async function loadEntityMap() {
     3:   const res = await fetch("/assets/data/entity_map.json", { cache: "no-store" });
     4:   const raw = await res.json();
     5:   return buildIndex(raw);
     6: }
     7: 
     8: function buildIndex(entities) {
     9:   const byId = new Map();
    10:   const aliasToId = new Map();
    11:   const regexes = []; // [{re: RegExp, id}]
    12: 
    13:   for (const e of entities) {
    14:     byId.set(e.id, e);
    15:     (e.aliases || []).forEach(a => aliasToId.set(String(a||"").toLowerCase(), e.id));
    16:     (e.patterns || []).forEach(p => { try { regexes.push({ re: new RegExp(p, "i"), id: e.id }); } catch {} });
    17:   }
    18:   return { byId, aliasToId, regexes };
    19: }
    20: 
    21: export function resolveEntity(text, idx) {
    22:   if (!idx || !text) return null;
    23:   const t = String(text).toLowerCase().trim();
    24:   const id1 = idx.aliasToId.get(t);
    25:   if (id1) return idx.byId.get(id1);
    26:   for (const { re, id } of idx.regexes) { try { if (re.test(text)) return idx.byId.get(id); } catch {} }
    27:   return null;
    28: }
    29: 
    30: export function getInternalTarget(entity) {
    31:   return entity?.internal?.url
    32:     ? { url: entity.internal.url, anchor: entity.internal.anchor || entity.labels?.canonical || "" }
    33:     : null;
    34: }
    35:

    37:   const reg = entity?.external?.region_overrides?.[regionCode] || [];
    38:   const pref = entity?.external?.preferred || [];
    39:   return [...reg, ...pref]; // [{domain,url}]
